_comment: Per-model block-level quantities (Table 2, updated). Uniform decoder blocks; embedding at N_0, LM head at a_S (not counted in per-block weight).

llama-3-8b._renamed_from: llama-3.2-8b -- a model that does not exist. Llama-3.2 ships 1B, 3B and the 11B/90B vision models, no 8B. L=32, d=4096 with 8 KV heads at head_dim 128 (chi 128 KB/token) is Meta-Llama-3-8B's shape, which Llama-3.1-8B shares exactly -- the simulator uses only L, d, omega and chi, so it cannot distinguish them. Table 3's 'Llama-3-8B' label was correct and the config key was wrong.

llama-3.2-1b._derivation: 16 layers x 8 KV heads x 64 head_dim x 2 (K and V) x 2 B (bf16) = 2048 B/layer/token; x16 = 32 KB/token. MEASURED on hardware: M3's migration test reports exactly 2048 B/block/token.
llama-3.2-1b._calibrated: Runtime-measured point, not extrapolated. Testbed TPOT 129.7 ms at S=2 across two Orin Nanos.

llama-3.2-3b._derivation: 28 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 head_dim x 2 x 2 B = 4096 B/layer/token; x28 = 112 KB/token.
llama-3.2-3b._calibrated: Runtime-measured point. Residency predicted 3602 MB vs measured 3608 MB per stage (0.2%). Testbed TPOT 182.7 ms at S=2. Does NOT fit on one 8 GB board -- the single-process reference is OOM-killed.

_flops_formula_DOC._comment: Per-block FLOPs. kappa_pf = 2*P*d^2 + 2*P^2*d (FFN + attn); kappa_dec = 2*d^2 + 4*d*(P+t) (FFN + attn over KV). P is prompt length, t is current decode step.
_flops_formula_DOC._note: DOCUMENTATION ONLY -- never read. The formulas are hardcoded in src/model_spec.py (kappa_pf_per_block, kappa_dec_per_block). Kept because they are the paper's Table 2, but renamed so nobody edits them expecting an effect. If these and model_spec.py ever disagree, model_spec.py is what ran.
